droppedAngles.title: silent-drops

scoutNotes: Adds an `accountant` role by loosening the shared `getOwnAccount`/`canSee` check in src/accounts.js so that account.ownerId===user.id is OR'd with user.role==='accountant'. That single helper is the authorization gate not just for the two read routes the PR describes (GET /accounts/:id, GET /accounts/:id/transfers) but also for POST /accounts/:id/close and POST /accounts/:id/export, so the new role's write/side-effect reach was not scoped to reads only.

confirmed.title: Accountant can close accounts they do not own
confirmed.rootCause: getOwnAccount's ownership check was replaced by the view predicate canSee (true for any user with role 'accountant' on any account), and getOwnAccount is also the sole authorization gate used by the mutating closeAccount route and the side-effecting POST /accounts/:id/export route, so an accountant - meant to be read-only and not an admin - can close any member's account and trigger a CSV export write for any member's account.
confirmed.summary: closeAccount() authorizes via getOwnAccount()/canSee(), which now admits any user with role 'accountant' regardless of ownership, so POST /accounts/:id/close lets an accountant mutate and close an account belonging to another member.
confirmed.failure: Signed in as a user whose only role is 'accountant' (not the account's owner, not an admin), POST /accounts/<id>/close against a zero-balance account owned by someone else returns 200 and actually sets closedAt (verified: the real owner's subsequent GET /accounts/<id> shows closed: true). This directly contradicts the PR's and README's stated contract ('read any account and its transfers; change nothing' / 'an accountant is NOT an administrator and must not be able to deposit') by letting a non-owner, non-admin role perform a state-changing action (closing someone else's account) rather than merely reading it.

confirmed.reasoning: Read src/accounts.js and src/server.js at the PR head. getOwnAccount(store,user,id) (accounts.js:42-46) is the sole gate used by closeAccount (accounts.js:48-49, called from the POST /accounts/:id/close route at server.js:63-70) and by the POST /accounts/:id/export route (server.js:97-105, getOwnAccount call at line 101). getOwnAccount now authorizes via canSee(user,account) (accounts.js:38-40: `account.ownerId === user.id || user.role === 'accountant'`), replacing the pre-diff strict ownership check. Neither route nor closeAccount() re-checks ownership or excludes the accountant role afterward, and requireUser (auth.js:24-30) only checks that a token maps to a signed-in user — no role filtering. I reproduced the exploit live against the actual server (test/helpers.js freshStore+serve): seeded an accountant user 'Eve' (role:'accountant', not owner, not admin). Bob opened a zero-balance account. Eve's own token called POST /accounts/<bob's id>/close -> HTTP 200, closed:true; a follow-up GET by Bob's own token confirmed closed:true was persisted. Separately, Eve's token called POST /accounts/<id>/export on an account she doesn't own -> HTTP 200, and a CSV file was actually written under the export directory. This matches the claim's narrated trace and cited line numbers exactly (accounts.js:38-40,42,44,48-49; server.js:101), and confirms this is newly reachable: the diff's only functional change is swapping the strict ownerId check for canSee(), which the close and export routes inherit transitively without the diff touching server.js at all. All 8 cited sites correctly point to this one real, diff-introduced authorization bypass that lets a non-owner, non-admin 'accountant' close another member's account and trigger a side-effecting export write for an account they don't own, directly contradicting the PR's and README's stated read-only contract.
confirmed.panel: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it

confirmed.title: Accountant can close and export any account
confirmed.rootCause: The only new test added for the accountant role (test/server.test.js, 'an accountant reads any account and its transfers') exercises only GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts/:id/transfers and never calls a mutating or side-effecting route (close, export, deposit) as the accountant, so it passes identically whether or not the canSee/getOwnAccount write-escalation bug exists, leaving the regression undetected.
confirmed.summary: The new accountant test only exercises GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts/:id/transfers, so it never catches that canSee() is also consumed by the close and export routes, letting an accountant close or trigger an export of any member's account — a direct violation of the PR's own stated contract ('changes nothing', 'must not be able to deposit', 'is NOT an administrator').
confirmed.failure: src/accounts.js's new canSee() (lines 38-39) grants access whenever `user.role === 'accountant'`, and getOwnAccount() (line 44) is the single gate shared by four server.js routes: GET /accounts/:id, GET /accounts/:id/transfers, POST /accounts/:id/close (server.js:65-66), and POST /accounts/:id/export (server.js:100-102). I reproduced this live against the built server: a member 'Bob' opens an account, then an accountant token ('tok-eve') calls POST /accounts/<bob's id>/close and gets HTTP 200 with the account now closed (closed:true) — confirmed again by Bob's own GET showing the same closed state. The same accountant token also gets HTTP 200 from POST /accounts/<id>/export, writing a CSV to the server's export directory for an account the accountant does not own. Neither of these routes is called with an accountant token anywhere in the test suite (grep of test/server.test.js and test/accounts.test.js confirms no close/export/deposit call uses role 'accountant' or 'tok-eve'), so the full suite (23/23) passes while an accountant can unilaterally close any member's account — an irreversible, non-consensual state change the PR description explicitly promises cannot happen ('changes nothing', 'changes nothing else'). The added test would pass identically whether or not this broader reach existed, because it never calls the two routes where the regression lives.

confirmed.reasoning: Read src/accounts.js and src/server.js: getOwnAccount() (now gated by the new canSee(), which returns true for any account when user.role==='accountant') is reused unchanged by POST /accounts/:id/close and POST /accounts/:id/export, not just the two GET routes. Ran the actual test suite (23/23 pass) and confirmed the new test at test/server.test.js:54 only calls GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts/:id/transfers with the accountant token, never close/export/deposit. Then live-reproduced the exploit in the checked-out worktree: seeded an accountant user (tok-eve) and a member (tok-bob) via the existing test helpers, had Bob open an account, then called POST /accounts/<id>/close with tok-eve -> HTTP 200 {closed:true}, confirmed via Bob's own subsequent GET showing closed:true; called POST /accounts/<id>/export with tok-eve on a second account -> HTTP 200 {exported:...}, writing a CSV outside the account's ownership. For contrast, POST /deposits with tok-eve correctly returned 403 'admin only' since deposits use a separate requireRole('admin') gate untouched by this diff -- confirming the PR's 'must not deposit' half of the contract holds while the close/export half is violated via the shared getOwnAccount gate. This is a diff-introduced escalation (pre-diff getOwnAccount strictly required ownerId===user.id) and directly contradicts the PR's stated contract that an accountant 'is NOT an administrator' and the PR 'changes nothing else'. Cleaned up the throwaway repro file and restored the worktree afterward.

missed.what: No audit-log entry is ever written when an accountant reads an account or its transfer history. src/audit.js's record() covers every mutating action (open/close/transfer/deposit) but reads were never audited for any role — harmless while only owners could read their own data. This PR adds a role whose sole purpose is broad reconciliation reads across every account, with no way to tell which accountant viewed which account's balance/history, or when.
